summary: Observation of the zigzag movement of an orange light point above the trees: lack of information.
description: In 2015, a witness reported an observation made in September 1967 (the exact date is unknown) at 9:00 PM. While waiting outside for a friend, he noticed a bright yellow-orange point just above the trees, moving from left to right over a short distance. Before each change of direction (there were four), the point remained stationary for two to three seconds. No unusual noise was heard. The observation lasted approximately 30 seconds, after which the point quickly disappeared into the distance. No trail was observed. No other reports were collected. This rather strange observation of a luminous ball moving very quickly in a zigzag pattern is reminiscent of some reports of ball lightning sightings. This old, unique testimony, with an unknown precise date, does not allow (despite good illustrations) for confirmation or refutation of this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Recent testimony of an old observation: multiple observations of luminous phenomena by a motorist on his night journey: lack of information.
description: Recent testimony regarding an earlier sighting for which the witness was unable to provide the exact date in their questionnaire. After a telephone conversation with the witness, the latter confirmed the date as March 19, 1967, and that the luminous phenomena reported on Radio Limoges occurred in the vicinity of La Chapelle-Taillefert in the Creuse department. On March 19, 1967, around 11:00 PM, a motorist leaving the village of Mortemart (Haute-Vienne) was intrigued by a luminous phenomenon in the sky. He stopped to observe for 10 minutes, in a southeasterly direction, a luminous object moving silently. The object made successive stops, and its intensity varied during the observation, preventing the witness from definitively identifying a disc-shaped form. The object eventually disappeared over the horizon. No unusual noise was heard. Resuming his journey, a few minutes later, the driver was again intrigued by a reddish glow passing low behind his car. A few kilometers further on, in the countryside, he observed a figure illuminated from within. The driver stopped and realized that this UFO appeared to land on the ground about twenty meters from the road. Despite their son's insistence, and because they were impressed, the witness and his wife continued on their way home as quickly as possible. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. This sighting took place on the evening of the referendum initiated by General de Gaulle. This account of a strange, distant phenomenon does not fit any of the classic misinterpretations. Because it was received long after the sighting, and because the witness is the only one, GEIPAN classifies it as a weak case, despite the good quality of the testimony. If other similar accounts were to emerge, this case could gain more weight. The witness told us by telephone that there might have been other similar accounts near Gueret. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" pending further reports.
